guide.anotherComputer: Choosing another computer doesn't move your work. If you can, commit and push the changes you want to keep, and copy any other local files you need before switching.
guide.caches: Clear caches and build output you can regenerate, such as package manager caches. Removing node_modules frees space too, but it needs a reinstall before the project runs again. Leave files you don't recognize alone.
guide.inspect: Check free space on the drive and inspect folder sizes on this computer (worktrees default to .factory/worktrees in your home folder). On macOS and Linux, for example, run df -h and du -sh ~/.factory/worktrees/* in a terminal, or df -i if df -h still shows free space: a disk also fills up when it holds too many files, and removing disposable ones, such as caches, frees it.
guide.prevent: To avoid filling up again, remove worktrees once their work is merged, and start unrelated work on a fresh computer.
guide.unreachable: Don't delete files you can't inspect. If this computer stays unreachable, or you can't open a terminal on it, contact Factory support.
guide.worktrees: Delete only worktrees that every session using them has finished with. Deleting a worktree closes the sessions working in it and removes the whole checkout. Commit and push what you want to keep, copy any local-only files you need (such as ignored .env.local files, which the confirmation's file counts don't include) outside the worktree, then check the confirmation before you delete.
